chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

Seven do not shorten the salat: the tax collector who moves about in his tax collection; the amir who moves about within his governorship; the merchant who travels in his trade from market to market; the shepherd; the Bedouin who seeks places of rainfall and where trees grow; the man who seeks game, intending by it worldly amusement; and the fighter who cuts off the road.

key_terms.التَّاجِرُ: the merchant whose travel is for ongoing trade
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the obligatory salat subject here to the ruling of completion or shortening
key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: hunting pursued here for worldly amusement
key_terms.الْأَمِيرُ: the ruler or governor moving within the scope of his authority
key_terms.الْبَدَوِيُّ: the desert-dweller who moves in search of rain and vegetation
key_terms.الْجَابِي: the collector who travels in the course of gathering dues or taxes
key_terms.الْمُحَارِبُ: the one engaged in hostile wrongdoing, here described as cutting off the road
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُونَ: performing the salat in shortened form during travel

ai.seo_question: Which travelers must perform the salat in full and not shorten it during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning categories of travelers who must perform the salat in full rather than shortened form during travel. It identifies those whose travel is habitual, occupational, or sinful, indicating that not every journey qualifies for qasr.
